capability.summary: Run one Python script and report sampled peak RSS, or report this wrapper's RSS
capability.description: With an existing script path, launches that file using the current Python interpreter with no forwarded arguments and busy-polls psutil RSS until exit. With no argument or a non-existing path, it reports the wrapper process's current RSS. It exports only a JSON metric envelope, not a profile file.
capability.problem_space: Coarse process-RSS observation for one executable Python script or the wrapper itself; not line-by-line profiling, leak detection, child-tree accounting, safe code analysis, or profile-file export.

constraint.io_signature: Input: optional script_path string at CLI position 1. Existing paths are executed as `[sys.executable, script_path]`; omission or a non-existing path selects current-wrapper RSS mode. Output: JSON envelope with child exit_code and peak_rss_bytes, or current_process_rss_bytes.
accepted_inputs: no argument to measure the wrapper interpreter's current RSS
an existing Python script path whose code is intentionally authorized to execute without extra arguments
constraint.output_shape: Existing script path after child exit: {status: "success", tool: "psutil", target: string, exit_code: integer, peak_rss_bytes: integer}, wrapper exits 0 regardless of child exit. No argument or non-existing path: {status: "success", tool: "psutil", target: null, current_process_rss_bytes: integer}, exit 0. Launch, permission, psutil, or wait failures are uncaught and may traceback; there is no structured timeout error.
limitations: executes arbitrary Python code from an existing path with the wrapper's permissions and inherited working directory/environment; the child may modify files, access the network, or have other side effects
a non-existing supplied path is not reported as an error and silently falls back to measuring the wrapper process
samples only the direct process RSS in a busy loop, excludes child processes, provides no timeline or line attribution, and is nondeterministic
captures but never drains child stdout/stderr, so a verbose child can block on full pipes; there is no timeout, termination policy, output forwarding, or profile-file export

output_contract.description: JSON envelope containing either sampled direct-child peak RSS and exit code or the wrapper process's current RSS; no profile file is exported.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run a Python script and sample its peak RSS
report the current wrapper process RSS

detect memory leaks or profile child process trees

export a memory profile file or capture child output
